2.content: What the toolbar icon, the popup and the activity layer show while an agent controls a tab, and how to turn the layer off.

6.content: How it stays out of the way

8.content: An agent works in tabs of your own browser, so the extension marks the tab it controls. The mark appears in the toolbar icon, the popup and the activity layer drawn over the page.

9.content:
| Icon                       | When                                  | Tooltip                      |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Dark, with a white pointer | Connected, this tab is not controlled | `oh-my-webbridge: connected` |

10.content:
| Icon                        | When                        | Tooltip                                               |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Dark, with an amber pointer | A session controls this tab | `oh-my-webbridge: session research controls this tab` |

11.content:
| Icon | When                      | Tooltip                                                      |
| ---- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Grey | Not paired, or connecting | `oh-my-webbridge: not paired`, `oh-my-webbridge: connecting` |

12.content:
| Icon                | When                                         | Tooltip                                                                      |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Grey with a red dot | Daemon not running, or the daemon refused it | `oh-my-webbridge: daemon not running`, `oh-my-webbridge: connection refused` |

13.content:
| Icon                 | When   | Tooltip                   |
| -------------------- | ------ | ------------------------- |
| Grey with pause bars | Paused | `oh-my-webbridge: paused` |

14.content: The amber pointer is set on the controlled tab only. Other tabs keep the connection state icon. The tooltip uses the interface language of the extension.

15.content: While connected, the popup starts with a row labeled "This tab". It reads "Not controlled" for an ordinary tab, "Session research" for a controlled tab, and "Session research is working" while an action runs. The row follows the active tab.

16.content: Below the row is a prompt for your agent with a copy button. It shows suggestions for the active tab in turn, a new one every six seconds, starting with the ones that fit the page best. The popup picks them from the address, the title and what the page holds, such as tables, form fields, code blocks, a video or selected text. The pointer or the focus on the prompt holds the current suggestion; once you edit the prompt, it keeps your text.

17.content: The layer is drawn in Chrome and Firefox, on tabs the session opened and on tabs it borrowed from you. It ends when the session releases or closes the tab. While it is drawn, the page shows:

18.content: An edge glow while an action runs, fading out shortly after it finishes.

19.content: The agent's pointer, with a tag that shows the session name. It moves to the centre of each element an action targets and stays at the last one. On light backgrounds the arrow is dark with a white edge, on dark backgrounds white with a dark edge.

20.content: A chip in the bottom right corner with an amber dot and the session name.

21.content: The amber-pointer icon as the favicon, in place of the page's own icons.

22.content: A focus frame around the element an action targets, with the action name above it: Click, Hover, Type, Select, Check, Focus, Scroll, Drag or Upload. The label moves below the element when the element sits near the top edge. The frame follows elements of the main document; while the session has an iframe selected, the page shows the glow, the chip and the pointer at its last position only.

23.content: The focus frame stays for a moment after the action finishes, so a run of clicks reads as one activity instead of a flicker of frames. A navigation replaces the document, and the layer is drawn again on the new page.

24.content: The layer is one host element with a shadow root. The page's styles do not reach its parts.

25.content: It uses `pointer-events: none`, so clicks, selection and hover reach the page underneath.

26.content: It is `inert` and `aria-hidden`, so screen readers and the page's accessibility tree skip it. `read_page` returns the page text without the chip, and `snapshot` does not list the layer.

27.content: Screenshots and PDFs are taken with the layer hidden, then it reappears.

28.content: The layer carries a 75-second lease that the extension renews every 30 seconds. If the extension stops renewing it, the page removes the layer by itself and restores its own favicon, so a stopped worker or a lost debugger session leaves no markings behind.

29.content: Under **Settings**, then **Pages**, turn off **Show agent activity**. The layer disappears from every controlled tab at once and is not drawn on tabs that sessions claim later. Agents keep working, and the toolbar icon and the popup row still show which session controls the tab. Turn the switch on again to draw the layer on the tabs that are still controlled.

30.content: The layer follows the system's reduced motion and reduced transparency settings: the glow stops pulsing, the focus frame and the pointer move without gliding, and the chip switches to a solid background.

32.content: How the omw daemon and the browser extension split work, and how a command reaches a tab.

41.content: Two processes make up oh-my-webbridge. The daemon `omw` is a Go binary that listens on `127.0.0.1:17373`. The extension runs inside Chrome or Firefox and drives tabs through browser APIs. Agents, the CLI and the SDK call the daemon over HTTP; the daemon calls the extension over a WebSocket.

42.content: The daemon holds state that outlives a browser window.

43.content: Authentication. Every request is checked against the token here, except `GET /ping` and `POST /pair`.

44.content: Routing. It keeps one connection per browser and sends each command to Chrome or Firefox.

45.content: Concurrency and deadlines. It admits requests, applies a timeout, and answers `busy` when a limit is reached.

46.content: Files. It writes screenshots and PDFs to the paths you give it, and reads upload files for Firefox, whose extension cannot read local files.

47.content: CDP front end. `GET /json`, `GET /json/version` and `GET /devtools/page/{tab}` present Chrome tabs to CDP clients, and `omw serve --cdp` passes `/devtools/browser` through to a native DevTools endpoint.

48.content: Session bindings, stored in `bindings.json` in the config directory.

49.content: The extension owns the browser side.

50.content: Task tabs and their tab groups, including borrowing a tab that already exists.

51.content: `snapshot` of the DOM and accessibility tree, and the `@e` references derived from one snapshot.

52.content: Input: click, hover, type, select, check, focus, scroll, drag and upload.

54.content: Firefox: WebExtension APIs. `page.js` is injected into the selected frame on demand, `webRequest` handles presets and headers, `tabs.captureTab` takes screenshots, and `userScripts.execute` runs `evaluate`.

55.content: Network entries and console records for each controlled tab.

56.content: The activity layer drawn over a controlled page.

57.content: Firefox answers some actions with `unsupported`, because its extension APIs have no equivalent. The differences are listed in Firefox.

58.content: One tab belongs to one session at a time. A session that creates tabs keeps them in its own tab group; a borrowed tab stays in your group and returns on release. A tab group is neither a cookie boundary nor a security boundary: every tab in the profile shares the same logins.

59.content: The daemon keeps at most one Chrome connection and one Firefox connection. It tells them apart by the WebSocket Origin. The extension's hello reports the browser, the browser version, and the session names the extension holds.

60.content: A command may carry a `browser` field. A session binds to a browser on its first command and keeps that binding until `close_session` succeeds. The binding is written to `bindings.json`, so after a daemon restart the session is routed back to the same browser. The next hello re-reports the session names, and stale bindings are dropped.

61.content: A session without a binding goes to Chrome when it is connected, and to Firefox otherwise. `/json/list`, `/devtools/*` and raw `cdp` need the Chrome extension; `/json/version` reports the version even with no browser connected. A second connection from the same browser is refused with 409.

62.content: Requests arrive as `POST /command` with a 2 MiB body limit, or as frames on the extension WebSocket. The daemon assigns a random ID to a request that omits one, and a response is matched only against a pending request with that ID on the same connection. A dropped connection ends every command in flight on it with `outcome_unknown`. After reconnecting, only new requests are accepted.

63.content: Commands for one session run in order, and different sessions run concurrently. The extension also queues per session and answers `busy` past 32 waiting commands. `close_session` and `dialog` run outside the session queue, on a reserve of 16 slots, so a stuck session or an open dialog can still be cleared. Page CDP connections keep the protocol multiplexing: a Fetch or Debugger continuation runs while another command on the same target waits.

64.content: The default timeout is 30 seconds and the maximum is 120 seconds. A request that passes its deadline returns `outcome_unknown`, and the SDK does not retry an uncertain command.

65.content: Chrome runs the extension background as an MV3 service worker. The worker keeps one WebSocket to the daemon, sends a ping every 20 seconds, and closes the socket after 45 seconds without traffic. A `chrome.alarms` timer fires every 30 seconds and reconnects when the worker was stopped. Retries back off from 0.5 seconds to 30 seconds with jitter. No offscreen document, silent audio or polling loop keeps the worker alive, and Chrome may still stop it at any point.

66.content: A debugger session survives the worker that opened it and stays attached to its tab. The next worker starts without the state that answers paused requests. On startup it detaches the debugger sessions it inherited from the previous worker, which releases any request paused there, and attaches again on the next command. Session metadata lives in `chrome.storage.session` rather than in worker globals. Page CDP sessions end with the daemon connection that opened them.

67.content: Firefox runs an MV3 event page, which the browser suspends after 30 seconds idle. WebSocket traffic does not count as activity, so the 20-second heartbeat also calls `tabs.query` while a connection is open. A 30-second alarm reconnects after a suspension. Reloading the background drops the `webRequest` listeners and the frame selection. Presets are installed again on that tab's next controlled navigation.

68.content: The daemon is reachable only from the machine it runs on, and the token is the only credential.

69.content: It binds `127.0.0.1:17373` and rejects a request whose Host is not `127.0.0.1`.

70.content: Web origins are rejected. Only `chrome-extension://` origins with 32 letters from a to p and `moz-extension://` origins with a UUID are accepted, and only on `/extension`, `/ping` and `/pair`.

71.content: The CLI and the SDK send the token as `Authorization: Bearer`. The extension sends it as a WebSocket subprotocol, `omw-token.<token>`, next to `omw.v1`. No token appears in the URL.

72.content: `GET /ping` reports the version without a token. `POST /pair` requires an extension origin and redeems the six-digit code for the token.

73.content: A pairing code is valid for 5 minutes and 5 attempts.

74.content: The config directory is created with mode 0700. `config.json`, which holds the token, is written to a temporary file and published atomically with mode 0600.

75.content: The token grants full control of the browser: page JavaScript in any tab, raw CDP, and file writes to the absolute paths you name. It does not isolate you from another process running as the same OS user, and the profile's cookies are available to every tab.

76.content: The Chrome extension has no `<all_urls>` host permission, no resident content script and no external message entry point. Firefox declares `<all_urls>`, which screenshots, request filtering, cookies and cross-origin frames need; `userScripts` stays optional and is granted in the setup page or under **Settings**, then **Pages**.

77.content: These are capacity guards, not a bound on RSS: concurrent screenshots and Chrome's own tab and network caches still add memory.

157.content: **The agent calls tools only through MCP.** Playwright MCP, Browser MCP, Chrome DevTools MCP, agent-browser, PinchTab and Playwriter run as MCP servers. oh-my-webbridge has no MCP server; an agent runs `omw call` as its skill describes.

158.content: **Windows.** The Kimi browser extension, Playwright MCP, Chrome DevTools MCP, agent-browser, Claude in Chrome and the OpenCLI desktop app support Windows. Playwriter supports WSL, and PinchTab publishes Windows binaries with limited support. oh-my-webbridge runs on macOS and Linux.

159.content: **Microsoft Edge.** The Kimi browser extension, Browser MCP and Playwright MCP with `--extension` work in Edge. oh-my-webbridge supports Chrome and Firefox.

160.content: **Installation from an extension store.** The extensions of Kimi, Browser MCP, Playwright MCP, OpenCLI and Claude in Chrome install from the Chrome Web Store and update automatically. The oh-my-webbridge extension loads as an unpacked folder in Chrome, and Firefox keeps it after a restart only when it is signed.

161.content: **Several browser profiles at once.** One Browser MCP daemon connects up to 8 browsers or Chrome profiles. The oh-my-webbridge daemon accepts one Chrome connection and one Firefox connection.

162.content: **A separate cookie store for each task.** agent-browser sessions, PinchTab profiles, `--isolated` and `isolatedContext` in Playwright MCP, and `isolatedContext` in Chrome DevTools MCP keep cookies apart. All sessions of oh-my-webbridge share the browser profile.

163.content: **No desktop browser**, for example in CI. agent-browser, Playwright MCP, Chrome DevTools MCP and PinchTab start their own browser, headless when needed. oh-my-webbridge needs a running Chrome or Firefox with its extension.

164.content: **Performance, memory and network debugging.** Chrome DevTools MCP records performance traces, runs Lighthouse and reads heap snapshots. Playwright MCP, Chrome DevTools MCP and agent-browser mock network responses.

165.content: **The full Playwright API on your signed-in tabs.** Playwriter runs Playwright code on the tabs on which you turn its extension on.

166.content: **Ready-made commands for popular sites.** OpenCLI ships adapters that return structured data from more than 100 sites.

167.content: **A model in the tool.** Claude in Chrome and the Kimi side panel run a task with their own model. browser-use runs a task with a model that you configure, and Stagehand adds AI steps (`act`, `observe`, `extract`) to a script. oh-my-webbridge carries out the commands of the agent you use and contains no model.

237.content: The dev server listens on port 3884. Pages are MDX in `docs/content/docs`. `docs/content/docs/meta.json` lists them in sidebar order, and a new page has to be added there. Every path starts with a language segment, for example `/en/sessions/`; the site root sends a reader to the first browser language. `pnpm --filter @oh-my-webbridge/docs build` produces a static export for GitHub Pages. 239.content: English is the source language. The Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) text is translated from it by hand. `pnpm run i18n` converts the zh-TW text to Simplified Chinese (zh-CN) and to the Hong Kong and Macau variants (zh-HK, zh-MO) with OpenCC, then formats the output with oxfmt. Edit only the English and zh-TW files: the script overwrites the others. `pnpm run i18n:check` fails when a generated file differs from its source, and CI runs it.

243.content: The zh-CN conversion applies the OpenCC phrase tables (`twp` to `cn`), then the Mainland software terms listed in `scripts/i18n.mjs`, for example 分頁 to 标签页 and 工作階段 to 会话. The zh-HK and zh-MO conversions change character variants only (`tw` to `hk`); OpenCC has no separate Macau standard.

244.content: Each key in `en.json` must also be in `zh-TW.json`, with the same `{placeholders}`; otherwise the script stops. A heading in a translated page keeps the anchor of the English heading, for example `## 選擇器 [#selectors]`, so links to a section work in every language.

246.content: Version numbers and release notes come from fragments, not from commit messages, and nothing is published to npm.

247.content: Add one file per user-visible change under `.changeset/`, named after the change. The front matter holds the bump: `patch` for a fix, `minor` for a capability, `major` for breaking behavior.

248.content: The body is a short H1 title followed by the result the user sees, migration or scope notes where they apply, and the PR link once the PR exists. Fragments are rendered as GitHub Flavored Markdown, so close every block, keep raw HTML to comments, and write links inline.

249.content: A PR that changes published inputs, such as source, build scripts, dependencies, the release workflows or the extension manifests, fails CI without a new fragment. Tests and internal docs can omit one. Editing an existing fragment does not count.

250.content: A push to `main` maintains a draft `release/next` version PR. Its workflow runs `scripts/release-pr.mjs`, which consumes the fragments with `scripts/release.mjs version`, synchronizes the package, lockfile, daemon and manifest versions, and writes `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/releases/<version>.md`.

251.content: After the version PR merges, the version workflow tags the `chore(release): prepare <version>` commit. The tag runs the release workflow, which rebuilds, audits every archive, uploads the assets, verifies their SHA-256 digests, and publishes the GitHub Release after that.

252.content: After the GitHub Release, the stores workflow (`.github/workflows/stores.yml`) submits `omw-<version>-chrome-mv3.zip` to the Chrome Web Store. It submits the unsigned add-on to addons.mozilla.org with a `git archive` of the tagged commit and build notes for the reviewers. Both packages are downloaded from the published GitHub Release and checked against its digests and `SHA256SUMS`. Each store publishes the version after its review. A version that a store already has is left unchanged, so a release can be rerun. Another Chrome version that is still in review or waiting to be published stops the Chrome submission.

253.content: The Chrome job runs in the `chrome-web-store` environment. Google Workload Identity Federation exchanges the job's GitHub OIDC token for a short-lived access token of the publisher service account. The identity provider admits only `stores.yml` of this repository in that environment, and no Google key is stored. The AMO job reads the API key and secret from the `AMO_JWT_ISSUER` and `AMO_JWT_SECRET` secrets of the `addons-mozilla-org` environment. Both environments deploy only from `main` and `v*` tags.

254.content: A manual run of the stores workflow from `main` prints the status of each store, which checks both sets of credentials. Store listings, screenshots and privacy answers are edited in the dashboard of each store.

255.content: Archives use zstd level 3 and extract with `zstd -dc archive.tar.zst | tar -xf - -C DIR`.

256.content: The project is licensed under Apache-2.0. `NOTICE` holds the notices, and `THIRD_PARTY.md` lists the bundled filter lists and npm packages. Extension builds ship the full license texts under `licenses/`.

258.content: Install the Firefox extension, pair it with the daemon, and see how its actions differ from Chrome.

267.content: The Firefox build is an MV3 extension for Firefox 153 and later. It pairs with the same daemon and exposes the same actions as the Chrome extension, with the differences listed under Actions. Where the Chrome extension uses CDP, the Firefox extension uses WebExtension APIs: page actions run in a content script, presets, network capture and extra request headers use blocking `webRequest` listeners, screenshots use `tabs.captureTab`, and `evaluate` uses `userScripts`.

268.content: Each release has two Firefox files. Check both against `SHA256SUMS`.

276.content: Firefox Release and Beta install only extensions signed by Mozilla. A signed extension stays installed after a restart.

277.content: Sign the extension on addons.mozilla.org as unlisted and self-distributed. Upload the unsigned `.xpi` in the AMO Developer Hub, or run `web-ext sign --channel=unlisted --api-key=<JWT issuer> --api-secret=<JWT secret>` in the extracted directory. `web-ext` writes the signed `.xpi` to `web-ext-artifacts/`.

278.content: In `about:addons`, open the gear menu, choose **Install Add-on From File…**, and select the signed `.xpi`.

279.content: AMO validates each submission before it signs it. Signing can take up to 24 hours, and each version needs its own signature.

280.content: Firefox ESR, Developer Edition, Nightly and unbranded builds install the unsigned `.xpi` when `xpinstall.signatures.required` is `false` in `about:config`.

281.content: Installing the extension opens the setup page (`app.html`), which lists the setup steps:

282.content: **Start the daemon**: `omw start`, or `omw service install` to start at login. The step completes when the page reaches the daemon.

283.content: **Pair this browser**: run `omw pair`. It prints a six-digit code that is valid for 5 minutes and 5 attempts. Type it into the pairing code field.

285.content: **Try it with an agent**: `omw install-skill ~/.agents/skills`, then ask the agent something.

286.content: **Access to all websites** is the `<all_urls>` host permission, requested at installation. You can turn it off under Permissions in `about:addons`. Without it, page actions, `screenshot`, `cookies`, `network` with `cmd: "start"` and `emulate` with `data` return `restricted_tab` and presets stop filtering requests. A `navigate` to a URL that answers 204 No Content or 205 Reset Content then waits until the command deadline. Turning the permission back on restores filtering.

287.content: **User scripts** is the optional `userScripts` permission. Choose **Allow scripts** in step 3, or under **Settings**, then **Pages**, and confirm the Firefox prompt. Firefox accepts the request only from a user action, so these buttons are the only place to grant it. Until it is granted, `evaluate` and `wait` with `expression` return `unsupported`.

288.content: **Pause** in the popup disconnects the extension from the daemon until you select **Resume**.

289.content: The daemon keeps one Chrome connection and one Firefox connection at the same time. A second connection from the same browser gets HTTP 409.

290.content: A command with `browser` goes to that browser: `omw call --browser firefox SESSION ACTION` on the command line, `connect(session, { browser: "firefox" })` in the SDK.

291.content: A command without `browser` goes to the browser the session is bound to. An unbound session goes to the only connected browser, or to Chrome when both are connected.

292.content: The first command the daemon sends binds the session to that browser. Bindings are stored in `bindings.json` and survive extension reconnects and daemon restarts.

293.content: `browser` naming the other browser returns `session_browser` (HTTP 409). A bound browser that is not connected returns `browser_offline`; the daemon does not move the session to the other browser. `close_session` removes the binding.

294.content: `/json`, `/json/list`, `/json/version` and `/devtools/page/*` use Chrome. With only Firefox connected they return `unsupported` (HTTP 501).

295.content: `omw status` and `omw doctor` print one connection line for each browser.

320.content: A Firefox extension cannot produce trusted input. `click`, `dblclick`, `mouse_click`, `hover` and `send_keys` dispatch `pointer*`, `mouse*` and `key*` events with `isTrusted` set to `false`. The page gets no user activation. Popups from `window.open`, file choosers, fullscreen and clipboard reads that the page starts from these events fail. `click` still calls `element.click()` afterwards, which runs the default action of links, buttons and form controls. `fill` and `key_type` use `document.execCommand` and produce trusted `beforeinput` and `input` events. `hover` does not set `:hover`, so a menu that opens from CSS `:hover` stays closed. `send_keys` accepts `Backspace`, `Delete`, `Enter`, `Tab`, `Shift+Tab`, `Control+A` and `Meta+A`. Other keys return `unsupported`.

321.content: The background runs as an MV3 event page. Firefox suspends an idle event page after 30 seconds, and WebSocket traffic does not count as activity. While the extension is connected it sends a ping every 20 seconds and calls `tabs.query`, which keeps the page loaded. An alarm every 30 seconds reconnects after a suspension. Session metadata lives in `storage.session`, which Firefox clears when it restarts.

322.content: A background restart drops the `webRequest` listeners and the frame selection:

323.content: `preset {cmd:"status"}` reports `none` for existing tabs until the next navigation of the tab applies the session preset again.

325.content: Extra request headers apply to new task tabs; existing tabs need `emulate {data}` again.

326.content: Firefox presets use the same modes, filter lists, engine and session settings as Chrome, and they apply only to task tabs. Page presets describes the modes and the bundled lists.

327.content: Each task tab gets its own blocking `webRequest.onBeforeRequest` listener, filtered by `tabId`. It receives the requests of every frame, including cross-process iframes, and there is no per-tab target limit. Each request is matched synchronously once the lists have loaded.

328.content: A preset change applies to existing task tabs immediately and the response reports `appliesOn: "immediate"`. Reconfiguration replaces the listeners and sends nothing to the page, so a busy page does not delay it. A navigation with an unchanged preset keeps the listeners and the status counters; a preset with `environment` set reconfigures on each navigation.

329.content: `zen` blocks requests by type: `images` covers image and image set requests, `fonts` covers fonts, `css` covers stylesheets, and `javascript` covers scripts. With `javascript: true`, the extension also adds `Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'none'` to the document and iframe responses of the tab. Inline scripts and event handler attributes stop running, and `<noscript>` content does not render.

330.content: `environment` is accepted but reports `environmentState: "unavailable"` with a reason. Network filtering continues.

331.content: A blocked top-level page leaves the tab on its current page, with no error page.

Firefox drops temporary extensions when it restarts. A permanent install needs a signature from addons.mozilla.org in self-distribution mode; submit `omw-<version>-firefox-mv3-unsigned.xpi` there. A source build loads `dist/extension-firefox`.

359.content: Installing the extension opens the setup page. The popup reopens it with **Open setup** when the browser is not paired, the daemon is not running, or the daemon refuses the connection.

360.content: Run `omw start`. It starts the daemon in the background and prints `started`, or `already running` when one is up. The step completes by itself once the page reaches the daemon; until then it reads "Waiting for the daemon on 127.0.0.1:17373".

361.content: Run `omw pair`. It prints a six-digit code such as `482 913`, valid for 5 minutes and 5 attempts. Type the code into the pairing code field. The extension saves the daemon token and shows "This browser is paired."

362.content: Install the agent skill with `omw install-skill ~/.agents/skills`, then ask the agent for a browser task, for example to read the active tab.

363.content: Firefox adds a step of its own before the last one, **Allow scripts**, whose button carries the same label. The `evaluate` action needs the optional user script permission; you can grant it there, or later under **Settings**, then **Pages**.

364.content: The extension pages, the popup and the toolbar tooltip use the language of the browser. To choose another language, open the language menu at the bottom of the side rail on the setup or settings page. The extension has English, Traditional Chinese (Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau) and Simplified Chinese.

366.content: On macOS the command writes `~/Library/LaunchAgents/app.oh-my-webbridge.plist` and loads it with `launchctl`. On Linux it writes `~/.config/systemd/user/oh-my-webbridge.service` and enables the unit with `systemctl --user`. The unit runs `omw serve` with the configuration directory used by the install command. Stop a daemon that `omw start` launched before installing the service, because the service starts its own. Stop the service through its manager:

367.content: `omw stop` asks a running daemon to exit and leaves tabs open. With the service installed, use the service manager so the daemon does not start again.

It refuses to overwrite an existing file, so delete the old one before installing again. `omw skill` prints the same guide. The guide tells an agent which commands to run, how sessions and tab ownership work, and which errors to expect.

372.content: `evaluate` returns the value of the expression.

383.content: A command from an agent or a script runs in your ordinary Chrome or Firefox profile, so pages keep that profile's logins, cookies and extensions. The daemon runs on the same computer as the browser and listens only on `127.0.0.1:17373`.

388.content: Open tabs in the background, in one tab group per session. The group title comes from `group_title` or the session name. Tab groups only separate tasks on screen; every tab shares the profile and its cookies.

408.content: Every oh-my-webbridge command names a session, an action and a JSON object of arguments. The tables on this page map common commands of other tools to these actions. Before you move a task, check Comparison with other tools for capabilities that oh-my-webbridge does not have.

409.content: Install the daemon and the extension, and pair your browser. See Getting started.

412.content: **Sessions.** Use one session name for each task, for example `checkout`. The first command opens the session. Its tabs open in the background, in one tab group. End the task with `close_session`. All sessions use your browser profile and its cookies.

413.content: **References.** A reference has the form `@e<generation>.<index>` and comes from the latest `snapshot` of the tab. A reference that starts with `@e` and comes from another tool or an older snapshot fails with `stale_ref`. A reference without `@`, such as `e12`, is read as a CSS selector. Take a new snapshot after a navigation.

414.content: **Locators.** The `selector` argument accepts CSS and text locators. Playwright locators map to these forms. `role=` matches the name exactly, while `getByRole` matches a substring unless `exact: true` is set. Chained locators and `.filter()` have no counterpart. See Selectors.

415.content:
| Playwright locator                                     | oh-my-webbridge selector     |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| `getByRole("button", { name: "Submit", exact: true })` | `role=button[name="Submit"]` |

416.content:
| Playwright locator     | oh-my-webbridge selector |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `getByText("Sign in")` | `text=Sign in`           |

421.content: **JavaScript.** `evaluate` takes an expression, not a function. Send `document.title`, or wrap the function in a call: `(() => document.title)()`. Code that uses `await` goes in an async function call: `(async () => (await fetch("/api")).status)()`.

422.content: **Files.** `screenshot` and `save_as_pdf` take an absolute `path` and return it. They do not overwrite an existing file.

423.content: **Deadlines.** A command fails after 30 seconds by default. The HTTP body field `timeoutMs` sets 1 to 120000 milliseconds.

424.content: **Firefox.** Some actions answer `unsupported` in Firefox. See Firefox.

494.content: In extension mode, the daemon lists page targets at `/json/list` and serves one tab at `/devtools/page/{tabId}`. Its `/json/version` has no `webSocketDebuggerUrl`. Playwright's `chromium.connectOverCDP` and Puppeteer's `puppeteer.connect` with `browserURL` read that field to find the browser endpoint (Playwright source, Puppeteer source). There are two ways to move such a script.

495.content: Native mode passes a browser endpoint through the daemon. Start Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port=9222` and a separate `--user-data-dir`, then start the daemon with the browser URL from `http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version`:

496.content: Connect Playwright with the token in `headers`, as shown in CDP. In Puppeteer, pass `browserURL: "http://127.0.0.1:17373"` and the same header in `wsOptions.headers`. The script then drives that separate Chrome, not the profile you use every day.

508.content: Control which network requests the tabs a session owns may make with the anti-ad, zen and none presets.

518.content: A preset is part of the session configuration. It applies to the task tabs the session owns, including tabs it opens later.

519.content:

| `anti-ad` | Bundled filter lists | Optional, off by default | Ordinary task pages |

522.content: `preset` stores the configuration for the session and applies it to the tabs the session owns. `navigate` accepts the same `preset`, `zen` and `environment` fields. It stores them once the navigation starts. From the command line:

523.content: A session that has not selected a preset uses `anti-ad`, the default for new task tabs.

524.content: The lists are compiled into the extension at build time. `pnpm run filters:update` downloads them and records the URL, SHA-256 value, date and original notices in `third_party/filters/sources.lock.json`. The extension does not fetch rules or updates from a third-party server, and it works offline.

526.content: AdGuard Base, with the EasyList duplicates removed, and AdGuard Tracking Protection

528.content: The enabled, non-regional default lists of uBlock Origin: filters, badware, privacy, unbreak, quick fixes, URLHaus and Peter Lowe

529.content: Regional lists and annoyance lists are not included. Packaged uBO scriptlets and redirect resources come from Ghostery's pinned copy.

530.content: The engine implements request blocking and exceptions. Redirects, response body and HTML rewriting, CSP directives and procedural cosmetics are not implemented. A page can therefore render differently than it does under uBlock Origin or AdGuard with the same lists.

531.content: `zen` adds resource type blocking to `anti-ad`. Each switch is a boolean, and `true` blocks that resource type.

532.content:
| Switch   | Blocks                       | Default |
| -------- | ---------------------------- | ------- |
| `images` | Image and image set requests | `true`  |

536.content: `javascript: true` also stops inline scripts and event handler attributes. In Chrome, script execution is disabled through CDP. In Firefox, the extension adds `Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'none'` to the document and iframe responses of the tab. `<noscript>` content then does not render, because the browser still reports scripting as enabled.

537.content: The restrictions cover network requests. Inline and data images, inline CSS and installed service worker caches are not affected. A site that needs stylesheets or scripts breaks under these switches. Select `none` or relax a switch and navigate again.

538.content: `environment: true` adds cosmetics and scriptlets from the bundled lists, guarded by the document hostname. It is off by default, and skipped in `zen` while `javascript` is on.

539.content: Registration happens before the target document loads, so the setting applies to the next document the tab shows. It does not alter a page that is already loaded. Navigate again. A cross-host redirect or an iframe from another host receives network filtering only, because the guard never injects a different host's rules.

540.content: Environment injection is not anti-bot fingerprint spoofing. A scriptlet that fails to parse or throws affects only itself. Status reports installation, not successful execution of every scriptlet. In Firefox, `environment: true` is accepted but reported as `environmentState: "unavailable"`, and network filtering continues.

541.content: `none` removes interception from task tabs. A raw CDP Fetch handler installed through `cdp` conflicts with a preset request handler on the same tab. Select `none` first.

542.content: Presets apply only to tabs the session owns. A borrowed tab is never filtered, and it keeps no preset state for the session that borrowed it. Preset options on a navigation that targets a borrowed tab return `borrowed_tab`.

543.content: `preset {cmd:"status"}` reads the current tab and returns:

545.content: `blocked` and `allowed` request counts since the preset was installed

546.content: `network`, whether interception is active on the tab

548.content: `fallback`, up to 8 reasons, each cut to 300 characters

549.content: Any other `cmd` value returns `invalid_args`. A configuration call returns `config`, a status entry for each task tab, `appliesOn` and `borrowedTabsExcluded`. `appliesOn` is `immediate; environment on next navigation` in Chrome.

550.content: Matching runs in the extension background, in one filter engine shared by every tab. Requests are not sent to the daemon.

551.content: Engine data is released 30 seconds after the last filtered tab stops filtering. The next preset loads it again.

552.content: Network and script restrictions apply to existing task tabs and frames immediately. Environment registration applies to the next document.

553.content: Reconfiguring a tab disables interception on every target of the tab first, so page requests continue while a busy frame delays the rest. Installing the new preset needs the current document to answer. Use `close_session` to recover an unresponsive page.

554.content: Navigating a task tab whose preset did not change keeps the interception and sends no reconfiguration commands. With `environment` off, status counters continue across the navigation.

555.content: If the lists fail to load, requests pass unfiltered and status keeps the reason. `zen` type blocking still applies.

556.content: Chrome intercepts at most 128 targets per tab. Additional frames fail open and status records the reason. Firefox has no per-tab target limit.

557.content: When Chrome restarts the extension worker, status reports `none` for existing tabs until a controlled navigation reapplies the stored session configuration. No site action is retried.

558.content: `pnpm run filters:update` downloads the upstream lists, updates the gzip files and `sources.lock.json`, and fails on a download error or an invalid response. The build fails on an integrity mismatch between a list and its recorded SHA-256.

559.content: The Firefox build uses the same modes, lists and session settings. Network filtering runs in blocking `webRequest` listeners, environment injection is unavailable, and a blocked top-level page keeps the tab on its current page. Firefox covers the differences.

561.content: What the extension and the daemon read, where the data goes and what they keep on disk.

567.content: The browser extension and the omw daemon run on your computer. The project runs no server and receives no data from either of them.

568.content: To carry out a command from the daemon, the extension reads data from the browser. Depending on the command, it reads:

569.content: the address, title and content of pages in the tabs a session uses, or in a tab that a CDP client connects to: text, the accessibility tree, element values, screenshots and PDFs

570.content: cookies and page storage, for the `cookies` and `storage` actions

571.content: the requests and responses of a tab while a session records its network traffic

572.content: the addresses and titles of open tabs, for the CDP target list (`/json/list`) and when a session looks for a tab to borrow

573.content: When you open the popup, it reads the address and title of the active tab. On a page that the extension can access, it also reads the page language, the structured-data types, the length of the selected text, and how many tables, form fields, code blocks, videos, images and articles the page has. The popup uses these values to rank prompt suggestions and does not send them anywhere.

574.content: After pairing, the extension connects to one address: the daemon at `127.0.0.1:17373` on the same computer. It sends each result there and to no other address. The daemon accepts connections from the same computer only and returns the result to the program that sent the command, such as an agent or a script. That program decides what happens to the data next; an agent can pass page content to its model provider.

575.content: The extension keeps the daemon token and its settings in the browser's extension storage. Session state lives in session storage, which the browser clears when it restarts.

576.content: The daemon keeps its configuration, including the token, and the session bindings in its configuration directory: `~/Library/Application Support/oh-my-webbridge` on macOS, `~/.config/oh-my-webbridge` on Linux, or the directory in `OMW_HOME`. Screenshots and PDFs go to the path given in the command, or to `artifacts` in that directory.

577.content: Files that the `download` action saves go to the browser's download folder.

578.content: The extension and the daemon contain no analytics, telemetry, crash reporting or advertising. The filter lists for page presets ship inside the extension; nothing is downloaded at run time.

579.content: Ask privacy questions in GitHub Issues.

671.content: `cdp` sends one Chrome DevTools Protocol command to the tab: `method`, `params`, and an optional `sessionId` for a child target. It returns the protocol result unchanged.

672.content: Two methods change the bridge's own state. `Runtime.disable` ends the frame selection of its session, and `Page.disable` without a session id invalidates the tab's `@e` references; the next snapshot or navigation re-enables the events.

684.content: `@e` references belong to one document generation. Each snapshot numbers its references under a new generation, a Snowflake ID in base 36. In Chrome, a new snapshot, a frame selection, a new main document (navigation or reload) or a change of the tab's URL invalidates them. A snapshot taken inside a selected frame also expires when that frame navigates, reloads, is removed, or the selection ends. Other iframes loading or navigating leave it valid. In Firefox, references live in the document that produced them; see Firefox.

719.content: Chrome DevTools Protocol access through the daemon, in extension and native mode.

727.content: The daemon exposes Chrome DevTools Protocol in two modes at `127.0.0.1:17373`, the same address and port as the rest of its API:

728.content: **Extension mode** serves page targets through `chrome.debugger` in the Chrome extension. It needs a paired Chrome extension and works with the browser profile you already have open.

729.content: **Native mode** is a WebSocket proxy to a Chrome browser endpoint you start with remote debugging. It is enabled with `omw serve --cdp`.

730.content: Every request needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, including WebSocket upgrades. Get the token with `omw connection`. The `Host` header must be `127.0.0.1`. Requests that carry a web `Origin` are rejected with 403.

731.content:
| Endpoint              | Method | Reply                                   |
| --------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `/json`, `/json/list` | GET    | The open page targets, as a JSON array. |

732.content:
| Endpoint        | Method | Reply                                             |
| --------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `/json/version` | GET    | A version object without a browser WebSocket URL. |

733.content:
| Endpoint                 | Method    | Reply                        |
| ------------------------ | --------- | ---------------------------- |
| `/devtools/page/{tabId}` | WebSocket | One CDP session for one tab. |

734.content: When only the Firefox extension is connected, these endpoints answer HTTP 501 with the error code `unsupported`. When no browser is connected, `/json` and `/json/list` answer HTTP 503, while `/json/version` still returns its object.

735.content: `id` is the tab id. The list covers non-incognito HTTP(S) and `about:blank` tabs that belong to sessions and tabs you opened, because the extension can attach to both.

736.content: The object has no `webSocketDebuggerUrl`, so a client that discovers targets through `/json/version` finds none in this mode.

737.content: Connect to `ws://127.0.0.1:17373/devtools/page/{tabId}` with the Bearer header on the upgrade request. Before the WebSocket is accepted, the daemon asks the extension to attach to that tab.

738.content: A tab another session is using answers HTTP 409 and is not taken over.

739.content: The tab is released when the client disconnects, when the tab closes, when the debugger detaches, and when the daemon stops or the extension pauses or disconnects. Clients can reconnect afterwards.

740.content: Events for the tab are subscribed before the attach starts, so events that arrive before the attach reply are still forwarded.

741.content: Messages use the CDP shape. Commands need `id` and `method`:

742.content: A reply carries `result`, or an error object with code `-32000`:

743.content: Events carry `method`, `params` and, when the event belongs to a child target, `sessionId`. Replies can arrive out of order; the original ids are preserved.

746.content:
| Limit                | Value      |
| -------------------- | ---------- |
| Deadline per command | 30 seconds |

748.content: An event larger than 32 MiB is not forwarded. The bridge emits `Inspector.detached` for that tab and closes the connection. The daemon also closes the connection for an event whose parameters exceed 256 KiB. A client that cannot keep up with the event stream is disconnected rather than silently losing events.

749.content: When the page reports `Inspector.detached` without a `sessionId`, the daemon forwards it and closes the WebSocket, which matches the behavior of Chrome's own page endpoint.

750.content: The `cdp` action sends one protocol command on the session's current tab, attaching the tab if needed. It is the same transport as a page connection, without the WebSocket.

751.content:
| Argument | Type     | Meaning                                       |
| -------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `method` | `string` | Protocol method, for example `Page.navigate`. |

752.content:
| Argument | Type     | Meaning                              |
| -------- | -------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `params` | `object` | Method parameters. Defaults to `{}`. |

753.content:
| Argument    | Type     | Meaning                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sessionId` | `string` | Child target session, for a flat session opened by `Target.attachToTarget` with `flatten: true`. Omitted, the command goes to the tab's root session. |

754.content: The action is available in Chrome only. Firefox answers `unsupported` with HTTP 501 and the message `cdp is not available in Firefox: Firefox has no Chrome DevTools Protocol`.

755.content: Two methods interact with the rest of the bridge:

756.content: `Page.disable` on the root session clears the `@e` references of that tab. The next `snapshot` or `navigate` enables Page events again.

757.content: `Runtime.disable` ends the frame selection of that session. Later commands run in the main frame until `frame` selects one again.

758.content: The URL must start with `ws://` or `wss://` and include a host. Otherwise the daemon refuses to start. Start Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port=9222` to get that URL from `http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version`.

759.content: In native mode, `/json/version` adds the browser WebSocket URL and reports the other transport:

760.content: `/devtools/browser` opens a WebSocket to that URL and copies frames in both directions, so every CDP domain and every browser-level target is available. It answers HTTP 503 while native mode is not configured (501 while only the Firefox extension is connected), and HTTP 502 when the configured endpoint cannot be reached. The upstream dial has a 10 second timeout.

761.content: Playwright can connect to the proxy:

762.content: Set `OMW_TOKEN` to the `token` value from `omw connection`. Playwright reads `/json/version` and uses the `webSocketDebuggerUrl` it finds.

763.content: Native mode does not replace extension mode. `/json/list` still lists targets through the Chrome extension, so without the Chrome extension it answers HTTP 503 (501 while only the Firefox extension is connected) even when the proxy works.

764.content: Extension mode carries page targets only. The browser target endpoint is not available, and the domains Chrome allows to `chrome.debugger` are a subset of the full protocol. See the `chrome.debugger` reference for that list.

765.content: Native mode forwards whatever the configured endpoint accepts; the daemon does not filter domains or methods.

766.content: Chrome does not accept `--remote-debugging-port` together with the default profile directory in current versions. Point it at a separate user data directory; see remote debugging.

767.content: CDP replies, events and the `cdp` action's result share the 32 MiB message limit of the rest of the bridge. The action's arguments, like any `/command` body, are limited to 2 MiB.

808.content: The token is 32 random bytes in hex, the same value that `config.json` holds. It authorizes every request other than `GET /ping` and `POST /pair`, including WebSocket upgrades and CDP connections. Treat it as a secret: do not paste it into issues, logs or pages.

878.content: How an agent splits work into sessions, how tabs are opened, grouped and borrowed, and the limits that apply.

880.content: A session stays in one browser

882.content: New tabs open in the background

888.content: A session is the unit of work in oh-my-webbridge. Every command names a session, and the daemon routes it to the tabs that session holds. Tabs opened by a session sit in a tab group titled with the session name or the title the agent passed, so a task's pages stay together and apart from the pages you use.

889.content: Give each task its own session name and reuse it for everything the task does. Tasks that run at the same time use different names. Each session keeps its own tabs, tab group, current tab, presets and frame selection. The browser runs commands from different sessions at the same time.

890.content: A session starts with its first command. Its name is 1 to 96 letters (including CJK), digits, `_`, `.` or `-`.

891.content: A session's first command decides the browser it stays in: the browser named by `browser`, the only connected browser, or Chrome when both are connected. Later commands for that session go there, even after the other browser connects. `close_session` removes the binding. A command that asks for the other browser fails with `session_browser`.

892.content: Each session has one queue. Commands for a session run one at a time, in the order the daemon receives them, so a click that follows a snapshot acts on the page that snapshot described. Sessions do not share a queue, and a page that responds slowly in one session does not hold another session.

893.content: `dialog` and `close_session` are answered outside the session queue, so they still reach a tab whose command is waiting. One session can have 32 commands running or waiting at once.

894.content: `navigate` opens a tab when the session has no current tab or the command sets `newTab`. The tab opens in the background and joins the session's tab group:

895.content: `group_title` sets the title of the group. A navigation that opens a tab can change it; otherwise the current title stays. The default is the session name.

896.content: The group is created collapsed, so task tabs do not widen the tab strip. Expand it to look at the pages.

897.content: A later `navigate` without `newTab` reuses the current tab. A session holds at most 32 tabs, task and borrowed together.

898.content: `list_tabs` returns only the session's tabs, with URL, title, active flag, group title and whether the tab is borrowed.

899.content: `find_tab` with `active: true` claims the tab that is active in the last focused window. The URL must match exactly or by hostname:

900.content: Without `active: true`, `find_tab` only looks at tabs the session already holds. A borrowed tab stays open, and `close_tab` refuses it with `borrowed_tab`. The session uses it and releases it when it ends. One tab belongs to one session at a time, and another session that asks for it gets `tab_busy`. Presets apply only to tabs the session opened. Borrow a tab when the task needs the page you have open; otherwise open a task tab.

901.content: `close_session` cancels the commands still running or waiting for the session, closes the tabs the session opened, and releases the ones it borrowed, which stay open. It removes the session's browser binding and drops what the session recorded on borrowed tabs: frame selection, network entries, console output and `@e` references. Closing a tab yourself removes it from the session; the session ends only with `close_session`.

903.content:
| Limit            | Value                          |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Tabs per session | 32, task and borrowed together |

904.content:
| Limit                    | Value                                                     |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Commands running at once | 128 per browser; `close_session` and `dialog` use 16 more |

905.content:
| Limit                | Value                 |
| -------------------- | --------------------- |
| Commands per session | 32 running or waiting |

908.content: When a limit is reached the command fails with `busy` and HTTP 429 instead of waiting. Reduce concurrency, or close sessions that are finished.

909.content: `timeoutMs` covers the whole request, including time spent waiting in the session queue. When it runs out, or when the browser disconnects in the middle of a command, the call returns `outcome_unknown`. The action may already have reached the page: a click may have happened, a form may be submitted.

910.content:
Observe the page before reusing a command. `snapshot`, `read_page`, the tab URL, `get` and the
network log show what the page did. Send a command again only when the state shows the action did
not happen, and never replay a payment, publish or submit automatically.

911.content: Task tabs and borrowed tabs run in your browser profile, with its cookies, sessions and logins. Sessions and tab groups organize tabs, not accounts: every session sees the same logins, and clearing cookies or site storage for one task clears them for the profile. Sign out of a site when the next task should start signed out.

925.content: 琥珀色指標只標在受控制的分頁上。其他分頁維持顯示連線狀態的圖示。工具提示使用擴充功能的介面語言。

926.content: 連線時，彈出式視窗最上方是標為「這個分頁」的一列。一般分頁顯示「未受控制」，受控制的分頁顯示「工作階段 research」，動作執行期間顯示「工作階段 research 執行中」。這一列會跟隨作用中的分頁。

927.content: 這一列下方是給 Agent 的提示詞與複製按鈕。提示詞會輪流顯示適合目前分頁的建議，每六秒換一則，最適合網頁的排在前面。彈出式視窗依網址、標題與網頁內容挑選建議，例如表格、表單欄位、程式碼區塊、影片或選取的文字。指標停在提示詞上或焦點在提示詞內時，會停在目前的建議；修改提示詞後，會保留你的文字。

928.content: 活動層會繪製在 Chrome 與 Firefox 中，涵蓋工作階段開啟的分頁，以及它向你借用的分頁。工作階段釋放或關閉該分頁時，活動層隨之結束。繪製期間，頁面會顯示：

929.content: 動作執行期間的邊緣光暈，動作結束後不久淡出。

930.content: Agent 的指標，附帶顯示工作階段名稱的名牌。指標會移到每個動作所針對元素的中央，並停在最後一個元素上。淺色背景上的箭頭是深色帶白邊，深色背景上是白色帶深色邊。

931.content: 右下角的標籤，帶有琥珀色圓點與工作階段名稱。

932.content: 以琥珀色指標圖示作為網站圖示，取代頁面自己的圖示。

933.content: 動作所針對的元素周圍有焦點框，框上方標示動作名稱：Click、Hover、Type、Select、Check、Focus、Scroll、Drag 或 Upload。元素靠近上邊緣時，標籤會移到元素下方。焦點框跟隨主文件中的元素；工作階段選取了某個框架時，頁面只顯示光暈、標籤，以及停在上一個位置的指標。

934.content: 動作結束後，焦點框會再停留片刻，所以連續的點擊看起來是一次活動，而不是一閃一閃的框。導覽會取代文件，活動層會在新頁面上重新繪製。

935.content: 活動層是一個帶有 shadow root 的宿主元素。頁面的樣式不會影響它的各個部分。

936.content: 它使用 `pointer-events: none`，所以點擊、選取與懸停都會抵達下方的頁面。

937.content: 它是 `inert` 且 `aria-hidden`，所以螢幕閱讀器與頁面的無障礙樹都會略過它。`read_page` 回傳的頁面文字不含標籤，`snapshot` 也不會列出活動層。

938.content: 擷取螢幕截圖與 PDF 時會先隱藏活動層，完成後再重新顯示。

939.content: 活動層帶有 75 秒的租約，擴充功能每 30 秒續約一次。擴充功能停止續約時，頁面會自行移除活動層並還原自己的網站圖示，因此即使 worker 停止或偵錯工具工作階段中斷，也不會留下任何標記。

940.content: 到**設定**，再到**網頁**，關閉**顯示 Agent 活動**。活動層會同時從所有受控制的分頁消失，之後才被工作階段認領的分頁也不會繪製活動層。Agent 仍會繼續工作，工具列圖示與彈出式視窗的那一列仍會顯示哪個工作階段控制該分頁。重新開啟開關，會在仍受控制的分頁上繪製活動層。

941.content: 活動層遵循系統的減少動態效果與減少透明度設定：光暈不再脈動，焦點框與指標直接移動而不滑行，標籤改用實心背景。

943.content: omw daemon 與瀏覽器擴充功能如何分工，以及一個指令如何抵達分頁。

952.content: oh-my-webbridge 由兩個行程組成。daemon `omw` 是 Go 二進位檔，監聽 `127.0.0.1:17373`。擴充功能在 Chrome 或 Firefox 內執行，透過瀏覽器 API 操作分頁。Agent、CLI 與 SDK 透過 HTTP 呼叫 daemon；daemon 透過 WebSocket 呼叫擴充功能。

953.content: daemon 保存的狀態，不會隨瀏覽器視窗關閉而消失。

954.content: 驗證：除了 `GET /ping` 與 `POST /pair`，每個請求都在這裡以 token 檢查。

955.content: 路由：每個瀏覽器保留一條連線，並把每個指令送往 Chrome 或 Firefox。

956.content: 並行與期限：daemon 決定是否受理請求，套用逾時，並在達到上限時回應 `busy`。

957.content: 檔案：daemon 把螢幕截圖與 PDF 寫到你指定的路徑，並為 Firefox 讀取上傳檔案，因為 Firefox 的擴充功能無法讀取本機檔案。

958.content: CDP 前端：`GET /json`、`GET /json/version` 與 `GET /devtools/page/{tab}` 向 CDP 用戶端呈現 Chrome 分頁，`omw serve --cdp` 則把 `/devtools/browser` 轉送到原生 DevTools 端點。

959.content: 工作階段綁定：儲存在組態目錄的 `bindings.json`。

960.content: 擴充功能負責瀏覽器端的工作。

961.content: 任務分頁與其分頁群組，包括借用已存在的分頁。

962.content: DOM 與無障礙樹的 `snapshot`，以及由單一快照衍生的 `@e` 參照。

963.content: 輸入：點擊、懸停、輸入、選取、勾選、聚焦、捲動、拖曳與上傳。

965.content: Firefox：WebExtension API。`page.js` 依需求注入所選框架，`webRequest` 處理預設集與標頭，`tabs.captureTab` 擷取螢幕截圖，`userScripts.execute` 執行 `evaluate`。

966.content: 每個受控分頁的網路項目與主控台紀錄。

967.content: 繪製在受控頁面上方的活動層。

968.content: Firefox 對部分動作回應 `unsupported`，因為它的擴充功能 API 沒有對應的功能。差異列於 Firefox。

969.content: 一個分頁同一時間只屬於一個工作階段。建立分頁的工作階段把它們放在自己的分頁群組；借用的分頁留在你的群組，並在釋放時歸還。分頁群組不是 cookie 邊界，也不是安全邊界：設定檔內的每個分頁共用相同的登入狀態。

970.content: daemon 最多保留一條 Chrome 連線與一條 Firefox 連線，並以 WebSocket 的 Origin 區分兩者。擴充功能的 hello 會回報瀏覽器、瀏覽器版本，以及擴充功能持有的工作階段名稱。

971.content: 指令可以帶 `browser` 欄位。工作階段在第一個指令時綁定到某個瀏覽器，並維持該綁定，直到 `close_session` 成功。綁定會寫入 `bindings.json`，因此 daemon 重新啟動後，工作階段仍會路由回同一個瀏覽器。下一次 hello 會重新回報工作階段名稱，過期的綁定會被丟棄。

972.content: 沒有綁定的工作階段，在 Chrome 已連線時送往 Chrome，否則送往 Firefox。`/json/list`、`/devtools/*` 與原始 `cdp` 需要 Chrome 擴充功能；即使沒有瀏覽器連線，`/json/version` 仍會回報版本。同一個瀏覽器的第二條連線會被拒絕，並回應 409。

973.content: 請求以 `POST /command` 抵達，本文上限為 2 MiB；也可以作為擴充功能 WebSocket 上的框架抵達。請求若沒有 ID，daemon 會指派隨機 ID；回應只會與同一條連線上帶有該 ID 的待處理請求配對。連線中斷時，該連線上所有進行中的指令都以 `outcome_unknown` 結束。重新連線後，只接受新的請求。

974.content: 同一個工作階段的指令依序執行，不同的工作階段並行執行。擴充功能也依工作階段排隊，等待中的指令超過 32 個時回應 `busy`。`close_session` 與 `dialog` 不經過工作階段佇列，使用 16 個保留名額，因此卡住的工作階段或開啟中的對話框仍然可以被清除。頁面 CDP 連線保留協定的多工處理：同一個目標上有另一個指令在等待時，Fetch 或 Debugger 的接續仍會執行。

975.content: 預設逾時為 30 秒，上限為 120 秒。請求超過期限會回傳 `outcome_unknown`，SDK 不會重試結果不確定的指令。

976.content: Chrome 以 MV3 service worker 執行擴充功能背景。worker 與 daemon 保持一條 WebSocket，每 20 秒送出一次 ping，並在 45 秒沒有流量後關閉該 socket。`chrome.alarms` 計時器每 30 秒觸發一次，並在 worker 已停止時重新連線。重試間隔從 0.5 秒退避到 30 秒，並加入抖動。沒有 offscreen document、靜音音訊或輪詢迴圈讓 worker 保持存活，Chrome 仍可能隨時停止它。

977.content: 偵錯工作階段會比開啟它的 worker 更長壽，並維持附加在分頁上。下一個 worker 啟動時，不會有處理已暫停請求所需的狀態。它在啟動時會分離從前一個 worker 繼承的偵錯工作階段，這會釋放在那裡暫停的所有請求，然後在下一個指令時重新附加。工作階段中繼資料存放在 `chrome.storage.session`，而不是 worker 的全域變數。頁面 CDP 工作階段會隨開啟它們的 daemon 連線結束。

978.content: Firefox 執行 MV3 event page，瀏覽器在閒置 30 秒後會將它暫停。WebSocket 流量不算作活動，因此在連線開啟期間，每 20 秒的心跳也會呼叫 `tabs.query`。暫停後，由 30 秒的 alarm 重新連線。重新載入背景頁會丟掉 `webRequest` 監聽器與框架選擇。預設集會在該分頁下一次受控導覽時重新安裝。

979.content: daemon 只能從它所在的機器連線，token 是唯一的憑證。

981.content: 網頁來源會被拒絕。只接受由 32 個 a 到 p 字母組成的 `chrome-extension://` 來源，以及帶有 UUID 的 `moz-extension://` 來源，而且只限 `/extension`、`/ping` 與 `/pair`。

982.content: CLI 與 SDK 以 `Authorization: Bearer` 傳送 token。擴充功能以 WebSocket 子協定 `omw-token.<token>` 傳送 token，並與 `omw.v1` 並列。URL 中不會出現 token。

983.content: `GET /ping` 不需要 token 即可回報版本。`POST /pair` 需要擴充功能來源，並以六位數配對碼換取 token。

984.content: 配對碼的有效期為 5 分鐘，可嘗試 5 次。

985.content: 組態目錄以 0700 權限建立。存放 token 的 `config.json` 先寫入暫存檔，再以 0600 權限原子性地發布。

986.content: token 授予瀏覽器的完整控制權：任何分頁中的頁面 JavaScript、原始 CDP，以及寫入你指定之絕對路徑的檔案。它無法把你與以同一個作業系統使用者執行的其他行程隔離，而且設定檔的 cookie 對每個分頁都可用。

987.content: Chrome 擴充功能沒有 `<all_urls>` 主機權限、沒有常駐的 content script，也沒有外部訊息入口。Firefox 宣告 `<all_urls>`，螢幕截圖、請求過濾、cookie 與跨來源框架都需要它；`userScripts` 維持為選用權限，在初始設定頁面或在 **設定** 下的 **網頁** 中授予。

988.content: 這些是容量防護，不是 RSS 的上限：同時進行的螢幕截圖，以及 Chrome 自己的分頁與網路快取，仍會增加記憶體用量。

1068.content: **Agent 只透過 MCP 呼叫工具。** Playwright MCP、Browser MCP、Chrome DevTools MCP、agent-browser、PinchTab 與 Playwriter 可作為 MCP 伺服器執行。oh-my-webbridge 沒有 MCP 伺服器；Agent 依技能說明執行 `omw call`。

1069.content: **Windows。** Kimi 瀏覽器擴充功能、Playwright MCP、Chrome DevTools MCP、agent-browser、Claude in Chrome 與 OpenCLI 桌面應用程式支援 Windows。Playwriter 支援 WSL，PinchTab 發布有限支援的 Windows 執行檔。oh-my-webbridge 在 macOS 與 Linux 上執行。

1070.content: **Microsoft Edge。** Kimi 瀏覽器擴充功能、Browser MCP 與加上 `--extension` 的 Playwright MCP 可在 Edge 中使用。oh-my-webbridge 支援 Chrome 與 Firefox。

1071.content: **從擴充功能商店安裝。** Kimi、Browser MCP、Playwright MCP、OpenCLI 與 Claude in Chrome 的擴充功能從 Chrome 線上應用程式商店安裝並自動更新。oh-my-webbridge 的擴充功能在 Chrome 中以未封裝資料夾載入，在 Firefox 中要經過簽署才會在重新啟動後保留。

1072.content: **同時連接多個瀏覽器設定檔。** 一個 Browser MCP daemon 最多連接 8 個瀏覽器或 Chrome 設定檔。oh-my-webbridge 的 daemon 接受一個 Chrome 連線與一個 Firefox 連線。

1073.content: **每個任務使用獨立的 cookie。** agent-browser 的工作階段、PinchTab 的設定檔、Playwright MCP 的 `--isolated` 與 `isolatedContext`，以及 Chrome DevTools MCP 的 `isolatedContext` 會分開 cookie。oh-my-webbridge 的所有工作階段共用瀏覽器設定檔。

1074.content: **沒有桌面瀏覽器**，例如在 CI 中。agent-browser、Playwright MCP、Chrome DevTools MCP 與 PinchTab 會啟動自己的瀏覽器，需要時以無頭模式執行。oh-my-webbridge 需要一個已安裝擴充功能且正在執行的 Chrome 或 Firefox。

1075.content: **效能、記憶體與網路除錯。** Chrome DevTools MCP 記錄效能追蹤、執行 Lighthouse 並讀取堆積快照。Playwright MCP、Chrome DevTools MCP 與 agent-browser 可以模擬網路回應。

1076.content: **在已登入的分頁上使用完整的 Playwright API。** Playwriter 在你開啟其擴充功能的分頁上執行 Playwright 程式碼。

1077.content: **常用網站的現成指令。** OpenCLI 附帶轉接器，可從 100 多個網站取回結構化資料。

1078.content: **工具內含模型。** Claude in Chrome 與 Kimi 側邊欄以自己的模型執行任務。browser-use 以你設定的模型執行任務，Stagehand 則在指令碼中加入 AI 步驟（`act`、`observe`、`extract`）。oh-my-webbridge 執行你所使用的 Agent 送來的指令，本身不含模型。

1079.content: Kimi 瀏覽器擴充功能：產品頁面、安裝指令碼、版本清單、`kimi-webbridge install-skill` 寫入的 Agent 指南，以及 Chrome 線上應用程式商店中擴充功能 2.0.33 的 manifest。

1080.content: Browser MCP：伺服器 README、工具定義、指令、貢獻指南、使用方式、運作方式。

1083.content: Chrome DevTools MCP：README、設定、進階用法、工具參考。

1084.content: agent-browser：README、指令、CDP 模式、工作階段。

1087.content: Claude in Chrome：Claude Code 文件、入門。

1090.content: 儲存庫結構、工具鏈、建置輸出、測試指令與發行流程。

1120.content: `make build` 執行相同的三個步驟，其中 `pnpm install` 帶 `--frozen-lockfile`。

1122.content: 檢查 `package.json`、兩份擴充功能 manifest，以及 `internal/bridge/protocol.go` 中的 `Version` 是否為同一個版本。

1123.content: 以 esbuild 將 `extension/src/worker.ts` 打包為 ES module，經過壓縮，目標為 `chrome156`。

1124.content: 將 `extension/src/firefox/worker.ts` 打包，目標為 `firefox153`，並將 `extension/src/firefox/page.ts` 打包為 IIFE。

1125.content: 在 `extension/ui` 執行 Vite 建置，並把 `popup.html`、`app.html` 與其資源複製到兩個擴充功能目錄。

1126.content: 以 resvg 從 `packages/brand/icons` 的 SVG 轉出工具列圖示與應用程式圖示。

1127.content: 編譯過濾清單，並複製所打包的 npm 套件與過濾清單來源的授權文字。

1128.content: 將 `sdk/index.ts` 打包為 `dist/sdk.mjs`，目標為 Node 24。

1130.content: 輸出為 `dist/omw`、Chrome 用的 `dist/extension`、Firefox 用的 `dist/extension-firefox`，以及 `dist/sdk.mjs`。Chrome 把 `dist/extension` 當作未封裝的擴充功能載入。Firefox 把 `dist/extension-firefox` 當作暫時性擴充功能載入。

1131.content: 彈出式視窗、初始設定頁面與設定頁面是同一個 Vite 專案。`extension/ui/vite.config.ts` 將 `popup.html` 與 `app.html` 列為輸入，以相對 base 建置，讓頁面能從 `chrome-extension://` URL 運作，並輸出到 `dist/extension-ui`。建置也會產生 `bundled-modules.json`，`scripts/build.mjs` 用它蒐集頁面套件中每個 npm 模組的授權。

1132.content: `app/app.tsx` 依 URL hash 選擇初始設定頁面或設定頁面，因此 `app.html#settings` 會直接開啟設定頁面。取自 coss registry 的元件位於 `extension/ui/src/components/ui`，保持 registry 提供的原樣；側欄、步驟清單等組合元件位於 `extension/ui/src/components`。儲存庫根目錄的 `design.md` 是這些頁面與文件網站的呈現規則。頁面從 `chrome.storage` 讀取連線狀態，並自行呼叫 `GET /ping` 與 `POST /pair`。WebSocket 由背景 worker 持有。

1133.content: `make check` 執行 `go vet`、型別感知的靜態檢查與格式檢查。`make test` 執行 `go test -race` 與 Node 測試套件。
